method: Independent read-only review of implementation and existing fixture. This review did not execute tests or simulate disk failure independently.

previous_critical_finding.description: Replacing the skin under the physics avatar would bypass the camera RenderProxy and split render-interpolated skin/source coordinates.
previous_critical_finding.fix_observed: Replacement retains old presentation parent, temporarily calibrates that parent at identity and restores it before returning; the fixture checks parent ownership and 48 rendered native-contact frames after a body swap.
previous_critical_finding.execution_verification: Separate release test reports owned by root/original_character; no passing runtime claim is made by this source review.

findings.evidence: Temporary file, flush/error and atomic rename precede committed-state mutation. Failure leaves preview open and old committed file/state intact. Cancel reapplies committed appearance and does not write a save.
Preview retains paused menu ownership. Escape routes to cancel, restores camera parameters and returns to the ordinary paused menu; later Escape uses the regular resume path.

Custom colors use per-instance duplicated materials and fresh ArrayMesh color arrays; source positions, skin weights, indices and original GLB resources are not assigned new values. Fixture separately snapshots NPC geometry/colors and asset hashes.

Preview can show baseline clothes while committed cancel restores the purchased top. Saving a changed jacket restores default outfit but retains inventory. Other edits retain the shop top. Active swimwear blocks customization; saved skin/hair apply to swim and street bodies.

Old native rig helpers stop processing and are detached/queued for deletion. Failed replacement cleans its helpers and retains the old skin. Player/capsule/source joints are reused and saved pose values are restored; gait fit refreshes against the replacement anatomy.
Grounded state, facility, vehicle, custody, active shop/swim and current action owners reject customization.

limitations: Read review cannot establish UI feel, real disk failure behavior, OS input or absence of frame jitter.
Rendered swap continuity and normal gameplay acceptance must use the frozen release fixtures and native visual evidence.
No claim of photoreal character quality is made.
